title: stratoshark: Inherit patch, build version and version extension from the project
description:
Since the Stratoshark source is released together with Wireshark patching and
building is done together.

In the release-4.6 branch Stratoshark inherits 0.9.x releases.

This prevents releasing Stratoshark with the same version again and again
with Wireshark point releases.

(cherry picked from commit de0949e22a8b1d37b769c3e0c753621f9654a4b5)


@geraldcombs Please skip the Wireshark 4.6.3 release and release 4.6.4 next to bump Stratoshark's version too. Alternatively we can do arithmetic at multiple places and it would be uglier to carry IMO.

notes.body: requested review from @geraldcombs
enabled automatic add to merge train when checks pass

> Please skip the Wireshark 4.6.3 release and release 4.6.4 next to bump Stratoshark's version too.

Is this really necessary? The ssv0.9.3 tag points to a commit in the master branch. You can't build the official 0.9.3 release from the 4.6 branch.

I think we have a different definition of "official". I see your point that there is one tagged commit with it, but if we build Stratoshark from any of the 4.6.x Wireshark tarballs it says "0.9.3" about itself despite being linked to parts that change between the Wireshark releases.

```
root@f4b0ae6d079b:/# ldd /usr/bin/strato | grep libw
	libwireshark.so.19 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwireshark.so.19 (0x0000707099528000)
	libwiretap.so.16 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwiretap.so.16 (0x000070709938c000)
	libwsutil.so.17 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwsutil.so.17 (0x0000707099339000)
root@f4b0ae6d079b:/# strato --version
Running as user "root" and group "root". This could be dangerous.
strato (Stratoshark) 0.9.3.
...
```

 This is wrong and also causes problems in distros as I explained in https://lists.wireshark.org/archives/wireshark-dev/202511/msg00017.html .
Stratoshark built from different Wireshark point releases must have different versions and this is one simple way ensuring that.

I agree with Gerald's initial reaction in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22637#note_2952948808, where we have 2 separate applications that share a repo.  They may need to be released at separate times, so they should be allowed to have separate versions.  Yes, you can build "the latest" Stratoshark from a Wireshark tag, but I don't think that makes it an official "Stratoshark release".  The same should be for building "the latest" Wireshark from a Stratoshark release. To me Wireshark tarballs "happen" to contain Stratoshark source, but should not be used for "official" Stratoshark releases.  I presume we'll have "Stratoshark tarballs" for Stratoshark releases (where you can build Wireshark at your own risk).
The build system should be able to recognize tags of the respective application and if they don't match, add the SHA-ID to the version.  i.e. If I build Wireshark on v4.6.2 tag, it's version should show as 4.6.2, but if I build Stratoshark on it, the Stratoshark version should be 0.9.3-24d5e2b5a (or similar).  If I build Stratoshark on the ssv0.9.3 tag, the Stratoshark version should be 0.9.3 and the Wireshark version should be 4.7.0-e665e93bd.  If there is a Stratoshark and Wireshark tag on the same commit, that would be an "official" release of both and their version shouldn't contain the SHA-ID.

If that 2 "separate applications that share a repo" it the project-wide agreement then they should be co-installable in any version combination which is not implemented properly in the CMake files nor in the release tarballs. There are no versioning rules like the one you propose established either. Using only SHA would not work because they are not guaranteed to order correctly, consider the 0.9.3-<SHA> versions varying in the 4.6.x Wireshark branch. There _could be_ something like that combined with dates or `git describe`, but there is nothing, that would work across distros and OS-es.
What I proposed and implemented in the MRs guarantees version uniqueness and proper version ordering with minimal complexity visible to end users.

If the stratoshark source is not and official release in wireshark tarballs I can (and should) drop it from Debian/Ubuntu packaging, because I completely misunderstood the situation and misled users about Stratoshark status.
Packaging Stratoshark separately safely would be challenging though because the package/file conflicts with Wireshark.

My exposure to Stratoshark has mostly been from the standpoint of refactoring/abstracting Wireshark code to be more generic to potentially support additional applications like Stratoshark. So "on Windows", I installed Stratoshark (with its standalone installer) and it's installed in a completely separate folder and structure from Wireshark.  Is that not the case on other platforms?  Are the other platforms trying to reuse the "shared libraries" (i.e. libwireshark, libwsutil) files?  If that's the case, to me the issue is the versions of the libraries, not the version Wireshark (although until the creation of Stratoshark, they were one in the same).  I would have presumed that Stratoshark would have its own installation folder and there wouldn't be any sharing of files to worry about potential conflicts.

On Debian and (I guess all) other distros Stratoshark and Wireshark use the same libraries and folders, thus if they go out of sync their conflicts need to be resolved either by renames or versioning, but the latter would be very messy.

Now I better understand your desire for this patch, but I see this as requiring syncing the library versions you're after more than the Wireshark application itself.  What do you think the path should be if a CVE (or other security critical issue) is needed for Wireshark (UI)?  Yes, 97+% of the time, the CVE is probably in a dissector (libwireshark), which would affect both applications, but are we then required to make a release with both applications?  As part of the discussion in !21941, I still would like to "long term" split out epan (dissection engine) and the dissectors into their own separate libraries which would mean more separation between Wireshark and Stratoshark.

But I'm also looking for consistency.  Should Stratoshark (on Windows) NOT be installed to a separate directory?  And then require additional subfolders to handle the application differences like colorfilter files, etc?  Because I'm really trying to have the "library code" (and supporting configuration files) NOT be superset between the two applications because they serve different purposes.  They just share a common "engine" that needs to sync its version.

With this patch I'm only after not distributing Stratoshark 0.9.3 with changing content.

All the libs and binaries are the same repo and we can't do separate releases. If there is a CVE in the now separated UI library the fixed release contains all libs and binaries (we refer to some of them as applications). This is why making separate Stratoshark and Wireshark releases are so artificial and challenging to manage.

IMO there should be only one bundle on Windows and Mac shipping both Wireshark and Stratoshark and a packaging scheme on Linux distros that builds and packages both, like it is currently done in Debian. That means that they would be installed with common paths everywhere and subfolders would be needed to separate the differences on Windows as well, indeed.

I think I see what you are aiming for and I'm not absolutely sure that it is worth the pain and complexity. If we had like 6 or 7 applications of similar complexity using the common UI, like in the classic MS Office, then yes, the library code probably should not be a superset of the needed features. Stratoshark has a way smaller problem domain, thus serving its needs from existing Wireshark library functionality is more manageable.

> IMO there should be only one bundle on Windows and Mac shipping both Wireshark and Stratoshark

That's not [how application bundles work on macOS](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/CoreFoundation/Conceptual/CFBundles/BundleTypes/BundleTypes.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/10000123i-CH101-SW19). You can ship multiple executables in a bundle, but there is a 1:1 relationship between the bundle name and the primary bundle executable. For example, we ship Wireshark, tshark, capinfos, and our other utilities in Wireshark.app/Contents/MacOS, but opening Wireshark.app only opens the correspondingly-named `Contents/MacOS/Wireshark` executable. Trying to add Stratoshark to the Wireshark.app bundle wouldn't work.

Indeed, I considered only the Windows installer, where shipping multiple programs worked for many years. I don't have any experience with building MacOS bundles.
I'm not trying to argue, just being curious. Are you sure that is not possible to add a proper Stratoshark app to the Wireshark bundle?
I found those by quickly googling:
https://medium.com/@schurigeln/bundling-multiple-apps-in-one-package-to-be-uploaded-to-the-mac-app-store-3d6268fc0396
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27359686/multiple-applications-in-a-single-bundle
Packaging them together would bring Stratoshark to a much wider audience immediately.

The first link describes shipping multiple application bundles from a single App Store entry. We distribute our packages directly and don't use the App Store. Both links describe helper applications, which are secondary applications that are launched indirectly from the main application and not directly launched by the user. For example, we ship the [Sparkle.app helper](https://sparkle-project.org/) with our bundles which handles automatic updates. It's launched by Wireshark and Stratoshark and if our users have to launch or otherwise interact with Sparkle.app directly, then that's a major bug.

Helper applications are hidden from the user at the operating system level. If we shipped a Stratoshark.app bundle inside the Wireshark.app bundle it wouldn't show up in the `/Applications` directory, it would be difficult and awkward to navigate to and open in the Finder, and it wouldn't show up in Spotlight searches.

Stratoshark really does need to have its own application bundle on macOS, just like any other standard application.

My understanding is the application bundles on macOS are more similar to Portable Apps on Windows, which do have some problems with the command line tools (#20095) and where Stratoshark probably needs its own installer. 

(Or somewhat like flatpak/snap/AppImage on Linux.)
marked this merge request as **draft**
I'm OK with merging this, but I'd prefer to do so after Wireshark 4.6.3 is released.

What would be Stratoshark's version in the Wireshark 4.6.3 tarball? It can be 0.9.3.1, but I'd prefer being consistent across operating systems and distros rather than hacking things in Debian only like I kind of do right now.
There is a lot of shared source, but should we intentionally not provide the "Stratoshark only" files (i.e mostly UI code) in the Wireshark tarball to prevent confusion?

That's a possible path, but I don't really see how would that benefit Stratoshark's adoption. I'm really not interested in doing extra packaging work because Stratoshark can't be released together with Wireshark due to missing sane versioning despite the files being there in the repo (and the Wireshark tarballs at the moment).

I'd rather wait in Debian/Ubuntu and flip shipping Stratoshark on when it starts shipping with versions synced with Wireshark as part of the Wireshark tarball as @geraldcombs planned in https://lists.wireshark.org/archives/wireshark-dev/202501/msg00002.html :

```
Maybe we should have three phases: A pre-1.0 phase with independent versions and
tag prefixes, a 1.0 phase with independent versions but with the standard "v" tag
prefix, and a post-1.0 phase, where we bump the Stratoshark version Sun-style[1]
to match the Wireshark version. The schedule would look something like this:
```

I'm trying to map out a release schedule for the coming year, likely leading to a Wireshark 5.0 + Stratoshark 1.0 release in late summer. I'd like to release Stratoshark 0.10.0 soon so that people can test the Procmon file parser and dissector, but releasing Wireshark 4.7.0 at the same time seems odd given that there isn't much that's new in the release notes.
I see that there aren't many no new features in Wireshark, but updated dissectors can be nice for many people thus releasing a development snapshot it always welcome IMO.
